biggestGap: Re-palette all 24 warden sprites onto the two-accent axis: every creature's lit pixels must land in violet (hue 240-300) or gold (hue 30-60), with element/affinity carried by VALUE and SILHOUETTE instead of hue. Right now the set paints in six hue families -- green (100-110deg: Halvane, Kellow, Verrow, Nettlejack), teal (180-200deg: Lorquin, Orrolek), blue (210-240deg: Corvidge, Quillow, Nimreth), magenta (300deg: Pellune, Sulmara, Tallow, Mirevail), orange/red (0-20deg: Baskarel, Ashquill, Cindren, Kethrivane) and brown -- and 19 of 24 sprites are more than 25% off-axis. That is the brief's stated automatic loss, and it is invisible to the current audit because the builder's palette check sampled computed CSS only, which cannot see a PNG.
evidence: CRITIC VERDICT. Replaces the builder self-assessment that previously occupied this file (which scored itself 78 and claimed 'only two hue families are painted'). Judged from pixels: five screenshots captured at 390x844 @2x over CDP, in progress/shots/wardens-codex-r1-critic-*.png.

PALETTE -- THE AUTOMATIC LOSS. Decoded all 24 bound sprite PNGs and binned every lit pixel by hue. Distinct 10deg hue families across the set: 0,10,20,30,40,50,100,110,180,190,200,210,220,230,240,250,260,270,280,300,340. Only Vharnys/Ythra (264deg) and Delvarn/Dunmoss (30deg) are on-axis. Halvane, Kellow, Verrow sit at a dominant 107deg -- literally green.

The 'Bound' filter is the proof shot (wardens-codex-r1-critic-grid-bound.png): all 12 owned wardens on screen at once render as a violet crown, a mauve stag, a violet hood, a pink moth, an orange boar, a BROWN HAMBURGER (Tessivar -- still reads as a burger despite the builder claiming it was re-authored into 'an orb crossed by a notched brass gear band'), a grey scarecrow, an orange bird, a teal mask, an orange flame, and two GREEN FROGS. That is a gacha rainbow, which is the exact failure mode the brief names.

Whole-screen hue histogram vs the bar: ours carries 1.38% magenta (300-315deg) and 1.15% orange (0-30deg) above the 0.2% threshold; reference/shots/ui-bar.png carries ZERO magenta and 0.20% orange. Ours also runs 2.64% gold against the bar's 6.60% -- the reference puts 2.5x more gold on screen than we do.

THE SUMMON MOMENT IS THE WORST CASUALTY. The Rite resolves to Halvane, a bright green goose, centred inside a gold-and-violet ritual seal. The one moment the piece is allowed to become an event, and the payoff shares no hue with the cabinet it sits in. It also leaves roughly 200px of dead vertical space between the rarity word and the diamond rule, which reads as an unfinished layout rather than as breathing room.

TAP TARGETS FAIL, INCLUDING THE PRIMARY CTA. Measured live: the SUMMON button is 114x36 and the three filter tabs are 117x30. The brief requires >=44px. The single most important control on the screen misses the mobile minimum by 8px.

THE MANDATED GATE IS VACUOUS FOR THIS PIECE. `npm run verify` reports 20/20 including 'no raw hex outside tokens.css', but tools/verify.mjs line ~75 iterates a hardcoded list of exactly three files (base.css, primitives.css, home.css). It never opens src/styles/wardens.css or wardens.html, which between them contain 13 raw hex literals (#000 x6, #050A10, #FFFFFF). The check passes without ever inspecting the piece it is supposed to be gating.

WHAT GENUINELY HOLDS -- the chrome is close to reference and should not be touched. Measured against the bar's three named traps: page ground luminance 9.1 vs panel 22.4 (the reference's #050A10/#13171B shift, correct); sealed-card names sit at luminance 199.3, which is exactly the reference's #C4C8CA secondary, so locked cards are distinguished by value and structure and NOT faded into illegibility; the empty progress track is the panel value, not a darker well.

GRID MECHANICS ARE CLEAN. 3 columns x 114px on 12px row and column gaps, scrollWidth 390 == clientWidth 390 so zero horizontal drift, all 24 sprites at natural 24x24 rendered at exactly 3x with image-rendering:pixelated, zero fractional scales. Cells are 117px tall, comfortably over 44.

THE DETAIL SHEET IS THE BEST SCREEN IN THE PROJECT and nearly ships as-is: two diamond-interrupted rules, an octagonal chamfered gold portrait frame, gold serif name, letter-spaced violet ASCENDANT with five violet pips, a chamfered beveled ASCEND plate, and checkpoint rungs with diamond bullets. Both of the reference's signature ornaments -- the chamfered gold button and the diamond divider -- get their second real use exactly as the brief asked.

MATH IS EXACT, NOT APPROXIMATE. Ran our xp.js against the published table in reference/melvor-math.md at 12 checkpoints (L=1,2,10,20,30,40,50,60,70,80,90,99): zero drift, including 13,034,431 at 99. xp(L+7)/xp(L) converges to 2.000 by level 70. The sheet's live figures are internally consistent too -- Vharnys at bond 62 shows 356,072/368,599 and 64.0%, and the 34,795 ascension cost equals xpAt(63)-xpAt(62) exactly, honouring the stated '1:1 from the pool' rule.

NAMING IS CLEAN -- NO AUTOMATIC LOSS. Grepped all src and root HTML for ~60 FFVI esper, character and place nouns. The only hits are inside src/js/engine/selftest.js lines 186-192, which is the project's own banned-word guard list rather than shipped content. All 24 warden names are invented.

BLIND A/B: laid the grid beside reference/shots/ui-bar.png with labels stripped. The reference is identifiable as the shipped product in under a second, and the tell is content, not chrome -- it holds two accents across a busy screen while ours fans across the wheel. Run the same test on the DETAIL SHEET alone and it is close to a tie. The chrome already clears the bar; the art asset layer is what loses.
